p: "If you will walk in My statutes, etc.,
I will give your rains in their season, etc."
"I will grant peace in the land, etc."
is from the accusation of the yetzer hara,
"There is no peace in my bones
and this is the essential, constant war
"'He makes even his enemies at peace with him'
but 'will make it at peace with you.'"
And as is said in the name of
רַבֵּינוּ ר׳ בִּינֶם זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
our master R' Bunim, zecher tzaddik livrachah,
that the meaning of "When you go out to war
as referring to the yetzer hara
is not a matter of derash and remez
for the war with the yetzer
And the Sifrei states (Eikev, Sifrei Devarim 43):
"'And you will eat and be satisfied;
lest your heart be seduced, etc.' (Devarim 11:15–16)
'Lest you eat and be satisfied, etc.,
That is: if it is not in holiness,
it will be only "the heart of a fool, to his left";
and when it is in holiness,
it will lead only to being
"the heart of a wise man, to his right" (Koheles 10:2).
"If you will walk in My statutes, etc.,
I will give your rains, etc."
that you recognize that Hashem Yisbarach
is the One who feeds and sustains;
and then the eating will not lead
and holiness to enter the heart.
For the food of Hashem Yisbarach is
and drink of the wine I have mixed" (Mishlei 9:5),
And this is what was requested by
Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him:
"and He will give me bread to eat" (Bereishis 28:20)
that he recognize that Hashem Yisbarach
is the source of the food;
and then the food will bring about
that he have only one heart
And this is "I will grant peace in the land"
from the accusation of the yetzer hara;
"and you shall lie down with none to make you afraid"
from the agitation of the yetzer hara,
that it will no longer enter to spoil.
In Tishrei they will be redeemed;
In Nissan they will be redeemed."
And we have said that they follow their own views:
not through teshuvah and good deeds.
And both are the words of the living God:
and "I will hasten it," if they merit
"today, if you will hearken to His voice"
between the rebukes of Toras Kohanim,
which are stated in the plural,
and in this there are levels,
as stated in the holy Zohar
"Not all masters of Torah are equal,
and not all prophets are equal, etc."
for even among prophets there are levels;
it is stated in the plural
of the rebukes of Mishneh Torah,
they are stated in the singular,
for in this there are no levels,
when it is the time of teshuvah,
"so that the year may end with its curses,"
and it be rectified through teshuvah,
so that they be redeemed in Tishrei
and those of Toras Kohanim before Atzeres,
for Atzeres is the time of rectification
in the aspect of "Come, eat of my bread";
and this is stated in the plural,
and every corruption from eating be rectified;
for this was the root of the blemish
at the time of the corruption
came the mixture of good and evil,
of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil;
Yet how can they all be true,
when the dispute is about a fact?
"And the Tree of Life in the midst of the garden,
and the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil";
the Tree of Life and the Tree of Knowledge,
were in the midst and inner part of the garden;
and had he tasted of the Tree of Life,
he would have sensed in all the fruits
the taste of the Tree of Life;
of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil,
and in everything he ate afterward
of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil.
And this is why it says "and all is true."
At first glance this would fit
אוֹ עַל כׇּל פָּנִים קוֹדֶם עֲצֶרֶת
which is the time of harvest,
but not on all the days of the year;
yet we say this berachah all year,
that what they said in the Gemara
"Bring before Me the Two Loaves on Atzeres,
so that there be blessed for you
according to the one who says,
"The tree from which Adam HaRishon ate
means that they should merit to rectify
was only from the fruit of the tree,
"For it is a statute for Yisrael, etc.,"
that all of a person's sustenance
and chok is an expression for sustenance.
the sustenance of each one of Yisrael,
as much as will benefit him
for the service of Hashem Yisbarach.
And this is "Provide me with my allotted bread" (Mishlei 30:8)
that Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him, requested;
although his daily meal was great,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּפָּסוּק (מְלָכִים א ה, ב–ג)
as is written in the pasuk (Melachim I 5:2–3),
was for him his allotted bread.
who was a son-in-law of the Nasi's house:
I have not drunk a revi'is of wine,
and likewise "who have not eaten beef"
to eat meat and wine for the sake of Torah,
and this was for him his allotted bread.
And this is what it says (Devarim 8:10):
and you shall bless Hashem your God
for although after the blemish it is written,
(as they said in the Sifrei there),
מִכׇּל מָקוֹם עַל יְדֵי בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן
that benefits the service of Hashem Yisbarach,
the rule of the yetzer hara.
And this is what we say in Birkas HaMazon:
and sustains all and does good to all"
that the eating be from the good.
And just as of Yerushalayim and the Mikdash, in space,
it is written regarding eating maaser:
"So that you learn to fear, etc." (Devarim 14:23),
so the eating of Shabbos, in time,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג כט, ב)
as stated in the holy Zohar (III 29b):
for Torah and the service of Hashem, blessed be He.
Some of them are like Shabbosos,
who need no work at all;
and some are like Yamim Tovim,
when work for preparing food is permitted:
and their eating, which is his allotted bread,
that is, even if we did not merit,
that it be allotted from Rosh Hashanah
that the eating be only from the good,
a person is judged every day,
so we pray that it be for good.
וְשָׁמַעְתִּי מֵרַבֵּנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה
And I heard from our holy master, zecher tzaddik v'kadosh livrachah,
that in the future the reading will be:
"Of every tree of the garden you may freely eat,
and the Tree of Knowledge — good;
and evil you shall not eat"
will be only from the good.
which is the time of Matan Torah,
which is called a Tree of Life,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה
as they said in Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu Rabbah
"'Tree of Life' means nothing other than Torah";
for the Torah is called the Tree of Life,
אִיתְּזָנוּ כׇּל שְׁאָר אִילָנִין לְתַתָּא וְכוּלֵּי
all the other trees below are nourished, etc.,
and therefore it is written of the Torah,
that it be from the side of the Tree of Life
then they read the parsha of the rebuke,
"so that the year may end with its curses,"
and a year begin with its blessings,
that our eating be only from the good
and from the Tree of Life.
And likewise of Shabbos it is written,
one senses the taste of the Tree of Life;
and about this the Arizal asked,
"May He reveal to us its taste,
which is in the twelve loaves"
Therefore on the Shabbos before Atzeres
